options.content:
Cost, tokens, cache, and request latency come from Claude Code OpenTelemetry. The collector renames metrics; if a panel is empty, open http://localhost:8889/metrics and edit the query. Short headless runs often miss a Prometheus scrape, so the JSONL file from the runner and `observability/data/claude-code-events.jsonl` are the per-run record.

Pass rate and cost per passing task are not Claude Code metrics. They appear after `python analyze.py results/runs.jsonl --prom observability/data/metrics.prom`. `run_id` is a metric label only in the resource attributes, which is fine on one machine and a bad idea at scale.

panels.title: Cost per setup
panels.description: Sum of claude_code.cost.usage, labeled by the setup resource attribute. Confirm the series name on the collector's /metrics.

panels.title: Pass rate per setup
panels.description: benchmark_passes / benchmark_runs from analyze.py. Empty until the summary file is written.

panels.title: Cost per passing task
panels.description: Sum of cost_usd_computed divided by the number of distinct tasks that passed. From analyze.py, not from the model provider.

panels.title: Tokens by role
panels.description: Token counter split by the role resource attribute (planner or builder process) and by query_source (main, subagent, auxiliary). Advisor tokens are not documented on this metric.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: cacheRead / (input + cacheRead + cacheCreation). Claude Code's input type excludes cache tokens, so this adds the three types instead of dividing cache reads by input.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: api_request duration_ms from Loki. Whole-run wall time is wall_ms in the JSONL. The Loki field names depend on how the collector maps log attributes; adjust this query after the first pilot.
